areas.name: Collection & Capacity Metrics
areas.description: Reports and analytics that describe the collection itself and physical capacity. Includes material volume and composition (by category, genre, format), shelving and shelf-space metrics, acquisitions and items inventory, location-based item counts, collection share, capacity views and trends (per branch, per system, and aggregate), data‑quality checks on bibliographic and item records (e.g., missing volumes, invalid item types, long call numbers), and configurable volume categories and groupings. Example topics: material volume reports, shelf items as source, new acquisitions as source, shelf space report, volume changes over time, collection share by genre/format, bib records with no volumes.

areas.name: Circulation & Transaction Analytics
areas.description: Reports and analytics about check‑out/check‑in activity, holds and hold workflows, loans (including inter-system/facility loans), renewals, transaction grouping and counts, transaction-level metadata (date/time/staff/workstation), return/turnaround metrics, fine/fee/payment reporting, and other transaction-based KPIs. Covers circulation counts by genre/format, percent renewals by branch, average return time, renewal likelihood, unfilled/stale holds, holds sent/received, intra-system loans, transactions per patron/library, detailed payments and voids, aged debt, and tracking of fines waived.

areas.name: Patron & Demographic Reporting
areas.description: Reports that describe patrons, their status and behavior, and outreach targets. Includes patron counts and trends (by age, profile group, home branch, county/city/zip), lists filtered by attributes (inactive, barred, expiring, specific note text), engagement metrics (OPAC/login/online holds/renewals/digital activity), survey and voter‑reg response rollups and lists, anonymization controls, exclusion rules, mailing-address outputs for outreach, and support for demographic and profile‑based reporting for outreach and program evaluation.

areas.name: Reporting Platform, Delivery & Compliance
areas.description: Capabilities and interfaces that enable, deliver and govern reporting across the system: canned and configurable report support, report scheduling and periodic reports, real‑time vs historical (warehouse/snapshot) delivery modes, selection and date‑range filtering, grouping and comparison views (per branch/system, local vs system average), configurable reporting levels (branch/system/custom levels), export/output columns, board and executive reports and cross‑tabulations, statutory compliance reports (e.g., Georgia Annual Report), report interfaces and testing/process definitions, and governance items (predefined report list, exclusion of patron‑facing functions from executive reporting, levels support).

areas.name: Ad-hoc Query & Report Builder
areas.description: Interactive query and ad‑hoc reporting tools including field selection, picklists, boolean and regex support, saved queries, manual selection from query results, pivot-style outputs and on‑demand exploratory reporting.

areas.name: Report Templates, Scheduling & Queue
areas.description: Report template creation, management and integrity (runnable templates), scheduling (recurring, ASAP, hourly/daily/yearly), report queue and prioritization, email delivery and recipient address book, and recurring report editing.

areas.name: Export, Integration & External Interfaces
areas.description: Output formats (CSV, Excel, HTML), export/warehouse approaches, vendor and third‑party interfaces (APIs, WorldCat), printable labels and external system integration (including file upload/download and API endpoints).

areas.name: Data Management & Purging
areas.description: Functions for identifying and removing records (weeding/purge), last-copy handling, delete/retain rules and criteria (time-based, activity-based, combined), confirmation steps, read-only purge reports, and safe batch processing for deletions.

areas.name: Item Transfer & Relocation Utilities
areas.description: Tools for moving items/records between locations: queries for candidate materials, generate pull lists, manual and batch relocation, change-location fields, preview/undo of transfers, auto-revert rules and transfer permissions.

areas.name: Transit, Missing & Damaged Items
areas.description: Reporting and workflows for in-transit, missing, damaged and in-transit aging items including thresholds, status‑based queries, sorting/filtering, transit labels, transit alerts and temporary event transfers.

areas.name: Audit, Compliance & Retention
areas.description: Comprehensive audit trails and retention support for actions (deletions, transfers, financial transactions), audit table design, retention policy enforcement, compliance logging (financial/audit), and denied-attempts tracking.

areas.name: Security & Access Control
areas.description: Role-based access control, roles and groups administration, fine-grained permissions for reports and templates, staff versus admin roles, OPAC/non‑OPAC access distinctions, and login methods (card/password).

areas.name: System Architecture, Performance & Scalability
areas.description: Server and infrastructure constraints (supported OS, browsers), relational DB backend requirements, background processing and caching, performance for large datasets, scaling to many locations, separate reporting DB/warehouse options, and deployment environments (dev/training/production).

areas.name: User Interface, Help & Accessibility
areas.description: Client access (web/Windows), browser compatibility, assistive technology and Section 508 compliance, HTML standards compliance, online/searchable help system, hover descriptions and printable outputs for staff use.

areas.name: Inventory, Collection & Weeding Metrics
areas.description: Inventory and collection management metrics such as volume counts, shelf space estimation (by count and dimensions), classification categories, weeding reports, last-copy reporting, material value, share by genre/format, and collection development support.

glossary.definition: A formatted output presenting selected data and aggregations, produced either on demand or on a schedule; may be canned, ad-hoc, or templated.
A saved, parameterized report definition that can be run directly or scheduled; includes field selection, filters, output format and permissions.
An interactive, user-constructed query against reporting data allowing field selection, boolean/regex filters and immediate results for exploration or export.
An intentional deletion process that removes records or items according to configured criteria and includes confirmation and audit logging.
A bibliographic record for which zero copies would remain at the source(s) if a specified copy/volume is removed; used as a critical purge/weeding criterion.
An operation that changes an item's owning or physical location (temporary or permanent), including associated status and transit tracking.
An item that has been sent from one location to another and is recorded as en route until it is received at the destination.
A registered user of the library system with an account record used in circulation, holds and demographic reports.
A single physical facility or logical library location within a system/consortium; the principal unit of location-based reporting.
A grouping of branches/ libraries that share administration, data or services; reporting may be scoped at the system or consortium level.
A security model where user permissions are granted through roles and groups rather than to individual accounts.
A recorded sequence of system events (who, what, when, where) used for forensic, compliance and change-history purposes.
Estimated physical storage capacity used by items, expressed in units derived from item counts or item dimensions for collection planning and capacity reporting.
The master metadata record describing a work (title/author/etc.); may be associated with zero or more physical copies/items.
A specific physical or electronic manifestation of a bibliographic record with its own barcode, status and location metadata.
High-level view of space or holdings limits across branches or system; used for big-picture planning and threshold alerts.
A report identifying items for removal from the collection according to configured criteria (usage, age, condition, last-copy rules).
An ordered list of scheduled or running report jobs showing position, submission time and status; supports prioritization and cancellation.

Texts fused so that the details of both are kept: The kept requirement covers the listed demographic dimensions and use in Ad-hoc Queries and Templates, but it does not state that age ranges are configurable per report, that age or age ranges can be derived from the birth_date field, or that filters are usable in saved queries. These distinct details would be lost.

merged_duplicates.name: Shared Report Folders
merged_duplicates.explanation: Both require shared report folders that govern staff access to Reports (and Templates) by folder. REQ-SEC-005 specifies additional permitted actions and role/group integration, but the core shared-folder access-control capability is repeated. Texts fused so that the details of both are kept: The kept requirement covers shared folders, administrator-controlled run permissions, Templates and Reports, and sharing across branches or teams. The removed requirement adds distinct permissions to view, schedule, and modify Reports, explicitly distinguishes folder-level from individual Report permissions, and requires integration with role and group membership; these details would be lost.

merged_duplicates.name: Multiple Output Formats
merged_duplicates.explanation: Both require support for multiple output formats for Reports and exports. REQ-EXP-001 adds specific format examples and export metadata, while REQ-TMP-016 adds format-selection and delivery details, but their core need overlaps. Texts fused so that the details of both are kept: The kept requirement covers multiple formats, scheduled/on-demand exports, and specific reports, but it does not state PDF or other format options, format selection in Template definitions, consistency with selected display fields, or integration with email delivery and combined-run behaviors. Merging would lose these distinct details.

merged_duplicates.name: Integration With ILS Modules
merged_duplicates.explanation: Both requirements express the need to integrate with an enterprise ILS, depend on its Acquisitions and Cataloging modules, and document the integration points. REQ-EXP-009 adds further details, such as authoritative core data and modular deployment. Texts fused so that the details of both are kept: The kept requirement covers the enterprise ILS dependency, Acquisitions/Cataloging integration, data reliance, and documentation, but the removed requirement adds distinct content: support for Management Processes, explicit data produced and consumed by those modules, interfaces with related modules, and simplified deployment for sites with full ILS stacks.

merged_duplicates.name: Card-Reader Optional Support
merged_duplicates.explanation: Both require branches to remain usable without card-reader hardware and describe card-based login as optional. REQ-SEC-007 already covers fallback username/password login and branch-level configuration, making REQ-SYS-020 redundant. Texts fused so that the details of both are kept: The kept requirement covers optional card login and username/password fallback, but the removed requirement adds distinct details: operation at branches without card-reader infrastructure, support for circulation and reporting workflows in those sites, and documentation of security or workflow differences when hardware is unavailable.

merged_duplicates.name: New Patron Count By Demographic
merged_duplicates.explanation: Both requirements report newly added Patrons over a period, support monthly comparison, demographic breakdowns, filtering by Branch, and export. REQ-PAT-013 is substantially a demographic-specific restatement of REQ-PAT-012. Texts fused so that the details of both are kept: The kept requirement covers monthly patron counts, demographic grouping, Branch scope, and exportability, but the removed requirement adds distinct details: administrator-specific filtering by other attributes, example demographic categories such as age or profile group, monthly comparisons, and use for program evaluation.

merged_duplicates.name: Time-Based Revert After Period
merged_duplicates.explanation: REQ-XFER-008 explicitly requires time-based automatic reversion after a configured period, while REQ-XFER-009 repeats that same capability with only additional configuration detail. Texts fused so that the details of both are kept: The kept requirement covers time-based reversion and audit logging, but does not explicitly state that the period can be configured per transfer or as a global default, that individual transfers can override the default, or that item metadata is updated.

open_issues.explanation: REQ-RPF-011 excludes patron-facing functions from management reporting interfaces, while REQ-UI-001 describes staff and patrons using the system for tasks including reporting and administration. Clarify that reporting and administrative activities are staff-only, or identify which reporting capabilities are available to patrons.

REQ-ADH-009 calls for exposing the full set of reporting fields, while REQ-SEC-009 allows administrators to hide or restrict access to specific tables and fields. These can coexist if field exposure is subject to role- and administrator-defined access controls, but that exception should be made explicit.

REQ-TMP-006 broadly bars Templates from displaying deleted items, while REQ-EXP-005 requires a report to list deleted last-copy items. Both can be met if the WorldCat report is treated as a dedicated deletion-audit exception, but that exception should be clarified.

REQ-TMP-006 broadly bars Templates from displaying deleted items, while REQ-DATA-003 requires a report listing deleted last copies. A dedicated audit-report exception can reconcile them, but the scope of the exclusion should be clarified.

Both govern retention of transaction data, but DATA-009 describes a configurable detailed-history window in days while AUD-004 requires retention periods to satisfy audit and legal policies, potentially for years. The scopes and effective retention periods should be clarified so the detailed-history policy does not purge records before applicable obligations are met.

DATA-009 calls for detailed transaction history for forensic purposes, while AUD-005 requires archived transactions to be anonymized so they cannot identify patrons. These can coexist by distinguishing the detailed retention window from anonymized archives, but the transition and what forensic detail remains available should be clarified.

Retention for audit purposes and anonymization of archived transactions can pull in different directions if audit needs identifiable transaction details. Clarify which records and fields must remain identifiable, and which may be anonymized, so retention and privacy obligations can both be met.

REQ-EXP-001 calls for exporting Reports and data, while REQ-EXP-007 requires Excel exports to suppress duplicate rows. Suppression could omit rows that are legitimately part of a Report’s results. Clarify whether deduplication is part of the Report definition or a separately scoped export option.

REQ-EXP-006 requires exported data to match the Report definition, whereas REQ-EXP-007 requires detected duplicate rows to be suppressed. These can pull in different directions if those rows are valid results under the definition; clarify whether validation is against the pre- or post-deduplication output, or how the Report definition accounts for deduplication.

Supporting consortium-scale reporting workloads while keeping reporting data in the main database may create contention or performance challenges. The requirements can coexist if the main-database mode is scoped to deployments where it can meet the scale and performance needs, with the stated mitigations.

critic_history.summary: The specification is broadly comprehensive, but it has several semantic duplicates, two explicit coverage gaps, and some terminology inconsistencies that require consolidation or rewriting.

Several significant issues remain: one requirement contains an internal contradiction and optionality conflict, one requirement is too vague to be testable, and the general transfer-reversion requirement semantically duplicates two more specific requirements. The documented open issues and stated coverage gaps were not re-reported.

The specification has broad source coverage and generally includes names, explanations, and priorities, but several requirements contain semantic duplication, one direct filtering contradiction, inconsistent vocabulary, and substantially over-merged scope.
